propositions: The caused_by auto-derivation mechanism (file-level git blame over impacted paths) produces unanswerable results without a provenance marker to distinguish blamed edges from explicitly supplied ones

Of 88 closed bugs carrying caused_by edges, the deriver reproduces 38 consistently, contradicts 6, and cannot re-derive 44 due to history drift or missing signals (no-fixing-commit, no-file-impact, no-majority)

On 8 bugs with independently proven origins, the deriver scored 0 correct matches, 1 confident wrong-target (naming an innocent producer), and 7 abstentions; the dominant defect shapes (unmet obligations, carrier commits, omissions) mostly fail closed rather than misattribute

File-level blame fails predictably on consumer-vs-producer contract violations because it names the producer innocent when the producer's code was correct at write time and the consumer's obligation was unmet
The 6 disagreements include 5 tickets sharing one recorded target but with 5 different derived targets, evidence of family-attribution scatter when blame is applied per-bug instead of per-family
